content.intro: {state} charges a filing fee to form an LLC and requires an annual report early each year. The yearly fee is not in the estimate yet, because we could not confirm it from the agency's own fee page.

howItWorks.text: The fees the Department of State charges for LLC filings are set in {state} law, including the fee to file the Articles of Organization.
The annual report must be delivered within a set window early each year, starting in the year after the LLC is formed.
An LLC that does not file the annual report can be dissolved, and it may not bring or defend a lawsuit in {state} courts until the report is filed and the fees and penalties are paid.
This page is held back from search engines until the yearly fee is confirmed from the Division of Corporations, so the total below leaves it out.

faq.q: When is the annual report due for a {state} LLC?
faq.text: It is delivered within a window early each year, and the first one falls in the year after the LLC is formed.

faq.q: What happens if a {state} LLC misses the annual report?
faq.text: It can be dissolved, and until it files and pays the fees and penalties it may not bring or defend a lawsuit in {state} courts.
